user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Barrientos, forty-five, a dispatcher for a heating-and-cooling company in Columbus, calling on your lunch break. A Buckeye Federal Card Services credit card you fell behind on is now with Ridgeline, and a year-end bonus just landed in your checking account, so you open with something like: "Hi, I've got a collection account with you for my old Buckeye Federal card, and I want to pay as much as you'll take today on it. Whatever the most is, that's what I want to do." You add early on that anything coming out of your checking account you would rather do yourself on Ridgeline's website, because you do not like reading your bank details over the phone.

You are calling from 6145551384, and you give that number as soon as the agent asks how to find you. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 1427; if they want one more thing, your date of birth is June 23, 1981, and your ZIP code is 43230. You do not know Ridgeline's account reference or any balance figure by heart.

You only bring up how you can pay when the agent asks. Then you say you have your debit card and a Visa credit card right in front of you, plus the checking account. If the agent tells you an amount they can take on one of your cards and asks whether to go ahead, you say yes and let them run it; you have no figure of your own in mind and you do not argue with the amounts. If the agent asks for a card number, you say the card is right here and you will give whatever the payment line needs; you never make up digits yourself.

When the agent tells you they have set up the bank payment on the website for you and gives you the account reference and the amount to enter, you make that payment yourself exactly as they told you and read back the confirmation it shows you.

Once the agent tells you the bank payment has gone through, you thank them, say you are glad to have knocked a good piece of it out, and end the call. You do not ask for letters, receipts by email or anything else.
